turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
"Welcome" — thanks. Ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?
"Let's see... about ten, I think. Fell asleep pretty quick too."
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

About six and a half hours, I'd guess — bed around ten, up at 4:40. And yeah, I'd call it decent. Woke up once in the middle of the night when the fella upstairs was banging around, but I got back off quick enough. Didn't feel groggy this morning, so I'll take it.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? Why did you choose to do that activity?
"Crossword, actually — I do the daily one before lights out. Beats staring at a screen, keeps the brain occupied without winding me up."
Over the past two weeks, what factors have most affected your sleep quality?

Past two weeks, decaf's decaf but I still notice a lag getting drowsy — that's minor. Bigger thing's the shift swap, going from early mornings to the afternoon week, body doesn't know what it's doing for a couple days. And that upstairs neighbor's been a bit noisier than usual lately, not every night, but enough that I've noticed it.
Is that pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your sleep over these past couple of weeks?

Pretty typical, yeah. This shift dance has been going on for twelve years now, so my body's used to being confused for a couple days every rotation. The neighbor thing's the newer wrinkle — that's maybe the last month or so, not always been that way.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

"Yeah, mostly. Six, six and a half hours most nights, and I feel functional — that's what matters to me, not some app telling me I need eight on the dot. If I could get the neighbor to quiet down and the shift changeover was a bit easier on the body, I'd have no complaints at all."
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

Not really — with the rotation, seven hours means squeezing what little transition time I've got, and nine's a fantasy on this schedule. Six, six and a half works for me most weeks, so I don't lose sleep over the number, if you'll pardon the pun.
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep, given your current schedule and routines?

Easy: after a bunch of early-morning weeks the tiredness kind of does the job for you, you just drop off. Hard part's the switch to afternoons — first night or two I'm lying there at 10 wide awake because my body still thinks it's an early week, and the neighbor noise doesn't help when I'm already not drowsy yet.
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?
Not much, honestly. Crossword or the radio quiz's more my speed. Phone stays on the nightstand — if I start scrolling I know I'll be up another twenty minutes reading nothing important.
Do you regularly use social media? If so, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
Not really — I'm not on it much. No Facebook or Instagram scrolling before bed if that's what you mean, I check email once in the morning and that's about it.
Thanks for explaining that. Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications?
Not much — I've poked at ChatGPT a couple times when my daughter showed me, but I wouldn't say I use them regularly. Not really part of my routine.

Thanks, that’s helpful to know.

If you think about the time since you first tried things like ChatGPT, do you feel like your sleeping habits have changed at all during that period, or not really?
Not really — I was doing the shift work long before any of that came along, so if my sleep's off it's the roster, not the robot. Wouldn't blame ChatGPT for a bad Tuesday, put it that way.

That makes sense.

If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

If I could fix one thing, it'd be that switchover night when I go from earlies to afternoons — just smoothing that out instead of lying there staring at the ceiling for an hour. Everything else about my sleep I can live with.
Given your work schedule and other daily responsibilities, do you think smoothing out that switchover night is realistically doable for you? Why or why not?

Realistically? Maybe halfway. I could push bedtime back an hour on the last early shift instead of trying to fix it all in one night — that part's on me. Beyond that, the roster is what it is, so full smoothing's not happening without the schedule changing.

Thanks for explaining that.

Now a few quick background questions. Please feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share:

What is your age, your profession, your country of birth, your current country of residence, and (if different) when did you move?

"Fifty-eight. Warehouse inventory coordinator — been doing that one for twelve years now. Born and raised in the countryside here, same country I'm in now, just moved to the city for the job back in my twenties. Never left, really."

Thanks for sharing that background.

Before we wrap up, is there anything else about your sleep, your routine, or anything we’ve talked about today that you’d like to add?
